Mr. Moudud Ahmed with Mr. Azizul Huq, Mr. Syed Ziaul Karim and Mr. Afsar Hossain Advocates ------ For the Petitioners. 
Mr. A.F.M. Shahid, D.A.G. with Mr. A.K.M. Shamsul Karim, A.A.G. and Mr. Giasuddin Ahmed ------ For the State.

Major (Rtd.) Md. Matiur Rahman and another ------ Petitioners.
Vs.
The State ------ Opposite Party.
full_judgment:
Habibur Rahman Khan, J.: This application for bail under Section 498 Cr.P.C. having been moved on behalf of Major (Retd) Md. Motiur Rahman and Md. Mofazzal Hossain accused in Pakundia P.S. Case No. 4(12)89 under Section 149/333/353/121/121A/122 /302 /307/201/379/427/435/436/114/34 of the Penal Code, a Rule was issued by this Court on 15.7.91 calling up on the Deputy Commissioner, Kishoreganj, to show cause as to why the said accused petitioners shall not be released on bail in the aforesaid case. 

 2. The accused petitioners along with several others are accused in Pakundia P.S. Case No. 4(12)89 under Sections 149/333/353 /121/121A/122/302/307/201/379/427/435/436/114 /34 of the Penal Code which was started consequent on the F.I.R. lodged by S.M. Shahabuddin, Officer, in-Charge of Pakundia Police Station on 13.12.89. The allegations made in the F.I.R. are that while constable Md. Joad Ali went to the 'Astana' of Pir Md. Motiur Rahman at village Simulia with by-cycle of one Biswa Nath Kundu, he was wrongly confined by the accused petitioner Md. Motiur Rahman and his men and thereafter Biswa Nath was also confined there while he went in search of the said constable. On 11.12.89 the police when went to rescue them were attacked by the followers of Md. Motiur Rahman and they opened fir indiscriminately and the police had to respond, as a result of the confrontation Md. Mahabbat Ali died. Thereafter, on 12.12.89 driver Abdur Razzak of the police party died of bullet injury. It is alleged that Major (Retd) Md. Motiur Rahman challenged the law enforcing authority with the intention of depriving the Government from the sovereignty of a portion of the territory of Bangladesh after waging war on 11.12.89 to 13.12.89 and in the fight, they, being defeated were arrested, by the police. 

 4. The accused petitioners are also accused in 4 other cases bearing Pakundia P.S. Case No. 6(12)89 and Pakundia P.S. Case No. 5(12)89 under Section 364/346/342/379/34 of the Penal Code, Pakundia P.S. Case No. 7(12)89 under Section 19(A)(F) of the Arms Act read with Special Powers Act, Pakundia P.S. Case No. 3(12)89 under Section 121/121A/302/201 of the Penal Code and in all those cases bail application, having been filed, Rules being Criminal Misc. Case No. 559/91, Crl. Misc. Case No. 553 of 1991, Crl. Misc. Case No. 560/91 and Crl. Misc. Case No. 562 of 1991 were issued by this Court and those, Rules having been heard simultaneously are being disposed of by separate orders in each case. The facts and circumstances in all the cases are almost identical. 

 5. Let us now take up the instant case being criminal Misc. Case No. 558 of 1991 arising out of Pakundia P.S. Case No. 4(12)89 for consideration of the prayer for bail. After taking us through the contents of the F.I.R. Mr. Moudud Ahmed, the learned Counsel for the petitioner, submits that the petitioner No. 1 is 4 retired Army Officer and a freedom fighter and after his retirement from service he has become a devout Muslim and has dedicated himself for the cause of Islam and he has large number of followers who are inspired by the teachings of the Holy Quran. It is submitted that the accused petitioner No. 1 developed a complex comprising of Mosque, Madrasha, Khanka Sharif and was living a peaceful life with his followers and some people became envious of such position of accused petitioner No. 1 and at their instance the police started operation as a result of which 21 innocent people of the locality were killed. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the accused petitioners are innocent and they were arrested under Section 54 Cr.P.C. at Kapasia and thereafter shown arrested in the instant case on 20.12.89. The learned counsel submits that the accused are innocent and have been implicated falsely in the case out of enmity and grudge by the designing persons. Besides the merit of the case, the learned counsel prayed for bail on the ground that out of the 60 persons arrested in the case, 58 have been enlarged on bail and there being no specific 'allegation of any overact against the accused petitioners so as to constitute offence under which charge sheet has been submitted, they stand on the same footing with those who have been released on bail and, therefore, there is no reason as to why they will be deprived of the same privilege of bail. It is further submitted that the accused petitioners are in custody for over two years without any trial and there is no knowing as to when the trial will commence. The case record having not as yet been sent to the Court of Sessions for trial. Therefore, the learned counsel submits that further prolongation of the petitioners in custody without trial will amount to punishment. Referring to the order passed by the learned Sessions Judge, the learned Counsel submits that prayer for bail of the accused petitioner was rejected on 28.3.91 on the ground of a prima facie case against the accused petitioners and also on the ground that their prayer for bail was rejected earlier. The learned Counsel submits that the submission of charge sheet only does not debar an accused from enjoying privilege of bail rather it neutralizes the apprehension of tampering with the evidence, the investigation being over. 

 6. Mr. A.F.M. Shahid, the learned Deputy Attorney General, appearing for the State, submits that the nature of allegations made in the F.I.R. being very serious and the charge sheet having been submitted, prima facie case has been made out against the accused petitioners. The learned Deputy Attorney General submitted that the accused petitioner No. 1 is a very powerful person having a large number of followers and if he is released on bail there is chance of his absconsion and tampering with the evidence. It is further submitted that the past conduct of the accused petitioner shows that he is in the habit of keeping himself away from the Court to avoid trial as a result of which trial was held in his absence in a previous case. To refute this point Mr. Moudud Ahmed produced before the Court the photo copy of the judgment of High Court Division passed in Criminal Revision No. 602/90 from which it appears that the accused petitioner No. 1 was convicted in a case trial of which was held in absentia but it was not due to the fault of the accused and, therefore, the prayer for condonation of delay in filing the appeal against the judgment and order of conviction passed in that case was allowed. 

 7. In support of his submission that the bail should not be withheld as a punishment, the learned Advocate for the accused petitioner cited the case of Manzoor and others Vs. The State, reported in P.L.D. 1972(S.C.) 81 wherein it is held: 

 "The High Court did not follow correct principles in refusing bail. It is obviously not correct to depend on the accused persons even in the matter of deciding the question of his bail. Bail in non-bailable cases is a matter within the discretion of the Court which has to be exercised with due care and caution on the facts and circumstances of each case. For an offence punishable with death or transportation for life, an accused charged with the same is not to be released on bail if there are reasonable grounds for believing that he has committed such an offence. The onus is on prosecution to disclose those reasonable grounds, and the Court to examine the data available in the case to find out whether reasonable grounds exist to connect the accused person with the crime alleged against him. The Court's belief on the point has to rest on the accusations made in the report to the police, the nature and the credentials of the evidence which the prosecution proposes to lead in the case and all the other relevant circumstances surrounding the occurrence. It is important to remember that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment. There is no legal or moral compulsion to keep people in jail merely on the allegation that they have committed offences punishable with death or transportation, unless reasonable grounds appear to exist to disclose their complicity. The ultimate conviction an incarceration of a guilty person can repair the wrong caused by a mistaken relief of interim bail granted to him but no satisfactory reparation can be offered to an innocent man for his unjustified incarceration at any stage of the case, albeit his acquittal in the long run. 

 8. In this case the learned counsel prays for bail also on the ground that 58 co-accused have already been enlarged on bail and these two accused petitioners stand on the same footing. 

 9. In the case of Abdul Gafur Sarder Vs. State and another reported in 35 D.L.R. (A.D.) 279, the bail was granted by the Appellate Division on the ground that the Co-accused who fired the fatal gun fire was granted bail in the case. The learned Counsel submits that 58 persons who stand on the same footing having been enlarged on bail, the same privilege may be granted to the accused petitioners. 

 10. From the reading of the F.I.R. and the charge sheet we do not find any reasonable ground which calls for taking a different view in respect of the prayer for bail of the accused petitioners before us. Since the charge sheet has been submitted, it cannot be said that reasonable ground exists that the accused petitioners will get the scope of tampering with the evidence. Without entering into the merit of the case, which may prejudice either side, we are of the view that long delay in holding the trial is a good ground for consideration of the prayer for bail of the accused petitioners. As, admittedly, the case record has not yet been sent to the Sessions Judge for trial, it is not known when the trial will begin and, therefore, we think it reasonable to allow the accused petitioners to be released on bail till the commencement of the trial. We leave it for the trial Court to see whether the accused petitioners should continue on the bail during the trial also. 

 11. On the facts and circumstances, we are, therefore, satisfied that it is a fit case in which the accused petitioners should be enlarged on bail till the trial commences. We, however, like to mention that whatever observations we may have made in disposing of the, application, is for the limited purpose of bail and we are not to be understood to have decided any matter touching the merit of the case.
